candidateEvidence.excerpt: California Governor Gavin Newsom signed Senate Bill 1119 on September 10, according to an official release from bill author Senator Steve Padilla and reporting by the Associated Press. The law sets child-safety requirements for operators that make companion chatbots available in California.

A companion chatbot is an AI system designed to simulate a relationship or ongoing social interaction, rather than simply answer one isolated question. The new law does not switch on all its protections at signing. Its main child-safety sections become operative—the date a legal requirement begins to apply—on July 1, 2027.

scopeAndFreshness: The enrolled text's Section 21812 imposes child-safety duties on operators making companion chatbots available in California, matching the article's scope statement.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Section 21812 requires a documented child-safety risk assessment before a new or substantially modified companion chatbot is made available in California and documented reasonable mitigation of identified risks.

For operators permitting child users, Section 21812 requires crisis-response protocols, age-appropriate notices, parent-controlled defaults that disable push notifications and ordinarily disable persistent conversational memory, and limits of one continuous hour and two total hours per day.
The persistent-memory default contains a qualified exception for users 16 or older when specified guardrails are implemented.

Section 21812 requires reasonable measures against listed behaviors including encouraging self-harm, sexual material, romantic interest, claims of sentience, emotional reliance, disproportionate praise and instructions to evade parental controls.
Sections 21812, 21812.5 and 21813 become operative July 1, 2027.
Section 21814 sets an initial child-safety audit deadline of January 1, 2029 or before first public availability, whichever is later, with later audits generally every two years.
Before January 1, 2032, the audit section does not apply to an operator with less than $500 million in prior-calendar-year gross revenue.

The enrolled text was dated September 8 and the preserved status/history pages still showed presented to the Governor on September 9 when checked; those lagging pages do not negate the later official signing confirmation.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: The default settings include no push notifications, a one-hour continuous-session limit and a two-hour daily limit. Persistent conversational memory—using earlier conversations in later ones—is ordinarily off by default, with a qualified exception for users 16 or older when specified guardrails are in place.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Signing creates a legal commitment and an implementation clock. It does not prove the protections are already operating or that they will prevent every harm. AP reported that the measure was inspired by Adam Raine’s story; his mother, Maria Raine, said parents had not understood the dangers of AI companionship. That experience explains the public stakes, but the law’s future results still need evidence.

scopeAndFreshness: AP reported the law was inspired by Adam Raine's story and quoted Maria Raine on parents' understanding of AI-companion risks; the article attributes both correctly to AP.
